questions.question: Q1. The Beer-Lambert law in Sub-Calc A predicts how much light is absorbed by the azobenzene dye. Which variable does it depend on?

answers.b: The light intensity, dye concentration, and absorptivity through optical depth εCx
answers.c: The temperature of the light source
answers.d: The color of the polymer film

explanations.a: Incorrect — concentration alone is incomplete; absorptivity and path length matter equally.
explanations.b: Correct — I_abs = I_0 (1 - e^-εCx) includes all three factors.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Beer-Lambert depends on material properties, not source temperature.
explanations.d: Incorrect — The law is wavelength-specific through ε, but not on film color.

questions.question: Q2. In Sub-Calc A, which two wavelengths drive the azobenzene photoswitching cycle?

answers.a: 365 nm UV (to *cis*) and 450 nm visible (back to *trans*)

explanations.a: Correct — 365 nm drives trans → cis isomerization, 450 nm drives cis → trans recovery.
explanations.b: Incorrect — The wavelengths must be more specific.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Those are used in Sub-Calc B and D, not azobenzene switching.
explanations.d: Incorrect — High-energy radiation would destroy the polymer.

questions.question: Q3. What material enables the local heating in Sub-Calc B (NIR skin-activated implant)?

answers.a: Copper wires embedded in the polymer
answers.c: Gold nanorods tuned to absorb 808 nm near-infrared light

explanations.a: Incorrect — Copper is not biocompatible for passive heating.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Resistive heating requires electrical current, defeating the wireless goal.
explanations.c: Correct — Gold nanorods convert 808 nm photons into local heat via plasmonic absorption.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Thermistors measure temperature; they don't generate it.

questions.question: Q4. In Sub-Calc B, the implant activates once the local temperature rise crosses which threshold?

explanations.a: Incorrect — That is too high for practical biomedical use.
explanations.b: Correct — The thermoresponsive material switches at ΔT_req = 25 °C above ambient.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Activation is measured as a *rise* above baseline, not an absolute temperature.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Boiling water would damage tissue.

questions.question: Q5. In Sub-Calc C, the magnetic torque on a ferromagnetic-loaded tip is τ = mB sinθ. What is m in this equation?

answers.b: The meter length of the coil
answers.c: The molecular weight of the polymer
answers.d: The effective magnetic moment of the particles

explanations.a: Incorrect — Torque depends on the magnetic dipole moment, not mass.
explanations.b: Incorrect — The coil is part of Sub-Calc D; here m is a magnetic quantity.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Polymer chemistry is separate from the torque calculation.
explanations.d: Correct — m = M_s V_particle is the net magnetic moment of all particles.

questions.question: Q6. What is the saturation magnetisation M_s for magnetite (Fe_3O_4) used in Sub-Calc C?

explanations.a: Correct — M_s = 4.8 × 10^5 A/m is the standard for magnetite particles.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Close, but not the value in the simulation.
explanations.c: Incorrect — This is too low for magnetite.
explanations.d: Incorrect — This is approximately double the actual value.

questions.question: Q7. Why can a magnetic field penetrate deep into the body in Sub-Calc D without significant attenuation?

answers.b: Because neurons amplify the magnetic signal
answers.c: Because the relative magnetic permeability of tissue is approximately 1 (no absorption)
answers.d: Because blood contains iron that conducts the field

explanations.a: Incorrect — While tissue is slightly diamagnetic, that does not explain penetration.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Neurons do not amplify passive magnetic fields.
explanations.c: Correct — Biological tissue has µ_r ≈ 1, so magnetostatic fields pass through unabsorbed.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Iron in hemoglobin does not meaningfully conduct quasi-static fields.

questions.question: Q8. In Sub-Calc D, the on-axis magnetic field from a coil falls off with distance as which power law?

explanations.b: Incorrect — This applies to point charges in electrostatics, not coil fields.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Magnetic fields in non-absorbing tissue do not decay exponentially.
explanations.d: Correct — The on-axis field B ∝ 1/r^3 far from the coil, causing steep power scaling.

questions.question: Q9. Of the three stimuli (light, magnetic, thermal) in Sub-Calc E, which one acts the fastest?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Photoswitching is limited by reaction kinetics (seconds).
explanations.b: Correct — Magnetic torque acts in milliseconds, viscosity-limited and magnetic-moment-limited.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Thermal actuation is the slowest, limited by diffusion.
explanations.d: Incorrect — They span roughly six orders of magnitude in speed.

questions.question: Q10. What physical process limits the speed of thermal actuation in Sub-Calc E?

answers.a: Thermal diffusion (heat spreading through the material)
answers.c: The viscosity of the polymer chains
answers.d: The electrical resistance of the heating element

explanations.a: Correct — Thermal actuation is diffusion-limited with time constant τ_thermal.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Photon absorption limits light actuation, not thermal.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Viscosity limits magnetic alignment speed.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Resistance is only relevant if the heat source is electrical.
